doc.title: Bill Mays interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 5, 2025

title: Opening and the Norton Museum of Art gig
summary: Rowe introduces Mays, who says he started professionally at 15. He describes recent Norton Museum programs: a history of jazz piano and one improvised to 80 works of art.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe for the Fillius Jazz Archive, and I’m very pleased to have Bill Mays with me this morning, composer, pianist, and a guy who seems to have been very busy for like 60 years.
Boy am I tired. Yeah, I’ve been busy. I started playing professionally when I was 15 and I’ll be 82 in February, so I’ve had a long career, mostly having a lot of fun.

I’d like to do a little compare and contrast here, looking at your itinerary on your website I noticed one of your last gigs was at the Norton Museum of Art. And can you just tell me a little bit about that gig?

Well it was a couple of Sundays ago, there’s a wonderful collection, very eclectic, small by comparison with big museums, the Norton Museum of Art in West Palm Beach. And I had done a program for them three years ago called “A Brief History of Jazz Piano” where I did about 22 piano players starting with Jelly Roll, going up to I think I ended with Herbie Han – no I ended with Renee Rosnes. But that was the program I did there three years ago. You’re asking about what I did a couple of weeks ago. I picked 80 of my favorite pieces of art from the collection and they put them up on a big screen for 60 seconds each and my bass player and I played music that was appropriate to each segment. I had divided it into nine segments: women, flowers, New York City, political protests, and we picked songs and played, and we did some free improvising too as we looked at the screen.
